helpful: The statpack's interim section now clears the 50-resolved floor for a Term-2026 cell, so a real scored baseline (30/225) was available — a big improvement over anchoring bare.
CourtListener docket-entries with date_filed__lte made it easy to read the originating court's record without risking exposure to this application's own disposition.
The frozen context's explicit ladder state (response_requested/referred_to_court/amicus_briefs) made the increment claims unambiguous to state.
gaps: No provisioned document text for interim cells: the application itself and the CA1 stay-denial order would have sharpened both the merits read and the ask; record/documents/ was absent.

fedcourts query has no application-kind or escalation-signal filters, so a generic --include-applications query surfaces mostly time-extension rows ranked by recency; a --substantive-only or --response-requested filter would make it useful for interim priors.

No sanctioned way to see whether a companion application exists on another SCOTUS docket without risking the outcome; I learned of the federal parallel application only via a committed sibling prediction. A provisioned related-dockets hint (case-linked, cutoff-bounded) would help interim cells.
notes: Forward cell run three weeks after the snapshot cutoff; the disposition likely exists at run time, so all live retrieval was self-bounded to pre-cutoff entries.
